text.title: Competitor Analysis Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding the Competitor Analysis methodology. Every rule pairs a binary check with sourced rationale, plus the universal skip-this-methodology gate. Folds in the former framework file: Five-step systematic framework: identify competitor types, map positioning, analyse across 8 dimensions, find gaps, define differentiation.

rule.statement: Identify all three competitor types: direct (same product, same audience), indirect (different product, same problem), and future (emerging or could pivot). Target 5-10 direct, 3-5 indirect, 2-3 future. Every future competitor needs a concrete signal.
rule.rationale: Analysing only direct competitors misses the substitutes customers actually use and the entrants who will arrive in 18 months. Discovery sources are listed in the section below.

rule.statement: Plot each competitor on a 2-axis matrix (price vs feature breadth) and identify empty quadrants or underserved positions before selecting your own positioning.
rule.rationale: Empty quadrants reveal market gaps; overcrowded quadrants signal where differentiation is hardest. Visual mapping surfaces the whitespace that a feature list alone obscures.

rule.statement: Analyse each competitor across all 8 dimensions. Do not skip dimensions — missing ones leave blind spots that surface in the gap analysis.
rule.rationale: A partial analysis produces a partial gap table. Investors and customers will probe the dimensions you skipped. The eight dimensions are listed in the section below.

rule.statement: Differentiate on a competitor weakness, not on feature parity. Scrape 1-star reviews and convert the top 3 complaints into your positioning message.
rule.rationale: Copying competitors produces table-stakes features. Converting their biggest complaints into your headline creates a concrete, testable claim that resonates with dissatisfied users already searching for alternatives.

rule.statement: Cite a URL for every factual cell (price, founding year, employee count); reject cells without sources.
rule.rationale: Sourced claims are auditable; unsourced cells are liabilities.

rule.statement: Run per-competitor snapshot tasks in parallel, synthesis serially. Cuts wall-clock by 5-8x and isolates per-competitor context windows.
rule.rationale: Dumping 10+ competitors into one prompt overflows context and degrades gap analysis. Each competitor's pricing page, review scrape, and feature list is independent. Parallelising collection then serialising synthesis is the only pattern that scales beyond 5 competitors without context degradation.

rule.statement: Pin target geography in every prompt and reject any competitor whose primary market differs from your target region.
rule.rationale: Without geography pinning, agents return competitors ranked by Google's global SERP, which skews toward US companies even when the user's market is EU or APAC.

rule.statement: Write a positioning statement in the canonical template form before finalizing the gap analysis.
rule.rationale: Forces the team to articulate the differentiation concretely and reveals whether the gap identified is actually usable as messaging. The template form is shown in `content/05-examples.xml`.

rule.statement: Apply this methodology only if all entries in `## Applies If` hold and none of `## Skip If` triggers; otherwise abort and route to the correct methodology.

rationale.source: F-066 spec — decision tree minimum form

rule.rationale: A misrouted methodology produces wrong-shape output; the explicit skip rule is the universal default branch from the decision tree.

section.title: Discovery sources
section.p: Sources for discovery: Google "[problem] solution", Product Hunt category search, G2/Capterra category browse, "Alternatives to [known competitor]", Reddit "What do you use for [problem]?", direct customer interviews.

section.title: Positioning matrix axes
section.p: Axes: Premium vs Budget (vertical), Narrow vs Broad feature set (horizontal). Quadrants: Specialized/High Value, Enterprise/High Price, Niche/Underserved, Mass Market/Crowded.

list.item: Product — what features exist, what is missing
Pricing — model, tiers, effective monthly cost for 1 user billed monthly
Traction — estimated users, revenue proxy, growth signal
Marketing — channels, content cadence, ad spend signals
Weaknesses — 1-star reviews, forum complaints, missing features

section.title: Gap types
section.p: Five gap types to identify: feature gap (they do not have it), quality gap (they do it poorly), audience gap (they do not serve this segment), price gap (they are too expensive for some), experience gap (UX or onboarding is painful).
